questions.q: In MS Word, the keyboard shortcut to change the case of selected text (cycling through UPPERCASE, lowercase and Capitalize) is:
questions.solution: Shift+F3 cycles the case of the selection through Sentence case, lowercase, UPPERCASE, Capitalize Each Word and tOGGLE cASE.
questions.shortcut: Three states at your fingertips = F3 (the 3 helps you remember).

questions.q: Sending e-mails that imitate a legitimate bank to trick users into revealing passwords is:
questions.solution: Phishing uses counterfeit messages/sites to 'fish' for credentials. Pharming needs no lure - DNS is poisoned so even correct URLs land on fake sites. Spamming is bulk unsolicited mail; defacement vandalises pages.
questions.shortcut: Fake mail asking for credentials = phishing, the umbrella term.

questions.q: The decimal value of the binary number 111010 is:
The IP address 127.0.0.1 is used for:
options: Loopback testing of the local machine
questions.solution: 127.x.x.x (typically 127.0.0.1 = localhost) loops packets back to the sender's own TCP/IP stack for self-testing.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

She said to me, "I will meet you tomorrow."
options: She told me that she will meet me the next day.
She told me that she would meet you the next day.
She said me that she would meet me the next day.
She told me that she would meet me the next day.
questions.solution: said to me → told me; will → **would**; you → **me** (listener); tomorrow → **the next day**. B skips the backshift; C leaves 'you' unconverted; D writes the impossible 'said me'.
questions.shortcut: Four checks: told + would + me + next day.

questions.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

Mumbai is / more bigger / than any other city / in the state.
questions.solution: *Bigger* is already comparative; adding *more* creates a double comparative: *Mumbai is bigger than any other city in the state*. Part 3 is correct — *any other* is exactly what the comparison needs, since Mumbai itself belongs to the group of cities.
questions.shortcut: Double comparative = instant conviction: -er and 'more' cannot coexist.

questions.q: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: Mischievous has **three syllables** (MIS-chi-vous) and ends **-vous**. Mischevious/mischievious insert an extra syllable — the classic error.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Please help the poor.
options: You are request to help the poor.
You are requested to help the poor.
questions.solution: A 'please' request converts to **You are requested to + V1**. B drops 'be' in the Let-form and loses the request tone; C gives a statement of fact; D writes the noun 'request' where V3 'requested' is needed.
questions.shortcut: please → You are requested to …; order → Let … be …

questions.q: **Kalamkari**, the art of hand-painting or block-printing cotton textiles with natural dyes, is chiefly associated with —
questions.solution: Kalamkari ('pen-work') is practised at **Srikalahasti** (free-hand) and **Machilipatnam** (block-printed) in **Andhra Pradesh**.

questions.q: In the T20 World Cup 2026 final, India's opponent was —
questions.solution: India beat New Zealand by 96 runs at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad. Sri Lanka co-hosted the event but was not in the final.
questions.shortcut: Hosts ≠ finalists — Sri Lanka is the trap option.

questions.q: Who was the **23rd Tirthankara** of Jainism?
questions.solution: **Parshvanatha**, a prince of Varanasi (son of king Ashvasena), was the 23rd Tirthankara; his symbol is the **snake** and he preached four vows. Mahavira (24th) added Brahmacharya.

questions.q: India's new series of national accounts (GDP) released on 27 February 2026 has which base year?
questions.solution: MoSPI released the **GDP series with base year 2022-23** on 27 February 2026 (replacing 2011-12), with a far larger deflator set. IIP followed the same base from 1 June 2026; CPI uses calendar year 2024.
questions.shortcut: New GDP/IIP base = 2022-23; new CPI base = 2024.

questions.q: How many zeros are there at the end of 250! (factorial 250)?
questions.solution:
Each trailing zero needs a pair (2, 5); 5s are fewer, so count the 5s.
$\left\lfloor \frac{250}{5} \right\rfloor + \left\lfloor \frac{250}{25} \right\rfloor + \left\lfloor \frac{250}{125} \right\rfloor = 50 + 10 + 2 = 62$.

questions.q: What is the value of $1^2 + 2^2 + 3^2 + \dots + 15^2$?
The angles of elevation of the tops of two towers from the midpoint of the line joining their bases are $30^\circ$ and $60^\circ$. If the towers are 60 m apart, the difference of their heights is:
questions.solution:
Each base is 30 m from the midpoint.

$h_1=30\tan30^\circ=10\sqrt3$, $h_2=30\tan60^\circ=30\sqrt3$. Difference $=20\sqrt3$ m.
questions.shortcut: Midpoint splits 60 into 30 + 30; heights are $30\times\frac{1}{\sqrt3}$ and $30\times\sqrt3$ → difference $20\sqrt3$ m. (Ratio check: heights are always 1 : 3 here.)

questions.q: What is the sum of all the factors of 360?
Select the related number: **25 : 49 :: 34 : ?**
questions.solution: Digit sum of 25 is 2+5 = 7 and 7² = 49. Digit sum of 34 is 3+4 = 7, and 7² = **49**. Both members share digit sum 7 — the answer is its square again.
questions.shortcut: When a and b look unrelated, compute the digit sum: many CGL analogies are (digit sum)² or (digit sum)×k.

questions.q: Which letter lies **exactly midway between E and U** in the English alphabet?
questions.solution: E = 5, U = 21. Midpoint = (5 + 21) ÷ 2 = 13 → **M**. (Check: 7 letters F–L on one side, 7 letters N–T on the other.)
questions.shortcut: Average the two positions; EJOTY gives 13 = O − 2 = M.

questions.q:
**Statement:** Advertisement: 'Learn to swim in just 15 days — join our summer swimming camp!'

**Assumptions:**
I. Some people want to learn swimming in a short time.
II. Nobody can learn swimming in less than 15 days.

Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
options: Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
questions.solution: I: the '15 days' pitch only attracts customers if people value quick learning — negate it and the advert loses its point, so I is **implicit**. II: the camp need not believe faster learning is impossible; it only claims 15 days is enough — **not implicit**. Answer: **Only I**.
questions.shortcut: An advert assumes its hook appeals to someone; it assumes nothing about rivals.
